id: title:EDsCODE:tag duckgres connections with application name

observations.behavior: Adds an explicit parameterized assertion that a caller-supplied `application_name` is preserved and included in the generated connection string.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows PostHog's managed warehouse backend to distinguish its own internal workflow connections from customer database clients when those customers connect directly. This supports observability and diagnostics without changing connector behavior.

observations.code_quote: ``application_name`` is forwarded to duckgres as a standard libpq startup
observations.behavior: Documents that the PostgreSQL client library will include this identifier in server-side analytics events, making it visible on DuckDB/PostgreSQL side.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides a mechanism for distinguishing traffic sources at the database level while remaining compatible with existing psycopg usage; no change to query results or ingestion correctness.

observations.behavior: Adds unit tests checking both default fallback and override cases of the new argument, including dev-mode and service-credential paths.
observations.posthog_connection: Establishes regression protection against accidental removal or misconfiguration of the forwarding path across multiple entry points.

observations.limitations: The patch does not demonstrate any change to query execution, result accuracy, or recovery handling. The benefit relies entirely on downstream visibility and diagnostic capability rather than functional improvement. No tier 3 systemic risk reduction or broader architectural dependency changes are shown.

review.limitations: The patch does not demonstrate any change to query execution, result accuracy, or recovery handling. The benefit relies entirely on downstream visibility and diagnostic capability rather than functional improvement. No tier 3 systemic risk reduction or broader architectural dependency changes are shown.
review.reason: This group adds an explicit caller-identifying parameter through several warehouse backend connection helpers, documented and tested. It improves observability and distinguishes internal PostHog workflows from customer connections without changing core behavior. This fits tier 2: substantive bounded implementation and checks present, but no evidence supports tier 3 (broader capability or systemic risk).
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to managed warehouse operations and diagnostics; helps distinguish PostHog-managed queries from direct customer database access when shared infrastructure is used.
review.uncertainty: Assessment depends on whether this identifier actually reaches Duckgres analytics and how it is consumed by support and alerting systems; that consumption is not demonstrated in the diff.
